A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LeFusion, with readable main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices. The broadened title and scope in v2 do not prevent matching retained methods and cardiac experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original Emidec segmentation and synthesis-quality experiments in Tables 1–2, supported by generated-image and mask visualizations.

after.justification: v2 reports original cardiac and lung-nodule experiments, including segmentation, synthesis quality and histogram-control analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: v2 adds histogram-conditioned texture generation through cross-attention and control-sphere conditioning for DiffMask size and location control (Sections 3.2–3.3). These change model inputs and generation procedures. Lesion-focused inpainting, joint multi-channel modeling and anatomical mask constraints already existed in v1.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates cardiac MRI on Emidec only. v2 retains Emidec and adds LIDC lung-nodule CT synthesis and segmentation, including generation on healthy lung backgrounds. This extends coverage to another organ, imaging modality and substantially different lesion texture distribution.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated latent Cond-Diffusion (L) comparator to cardiac segmentation and synthesis-quality comparisons, and Copy-Paste to the LIDC copied-mask comparison. Chen et al. (2024) was discussed in v1 but was not a separate evaluated table entry. LeFusion-S becoming LeFusion and the association of RePaint with Blended-Diffusion do not establish additional comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds SwinUNETR alongside nnU-Net and NSD alongside Dice, plus LIDC training/test splits and copied-mask experiments. New analyses compare paired generations across 100 subsets and examine histograms from 20 sampled cases. The Emidec split and augmentation quantities remain unchanged; newly disclosed training budgets do not establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds comparisons with and without histogram conditioning, texture-distribution clustering, paired-generation diversity analysis (Figure 6), predicted-versus-observed histogram analysis (Appendix C), and control-sphere mask examples. These investigate texture control and failure mechanisms beyond v1's retained joint-modeling, mask-generation and augmentation-volume comparisons.

E5.justification: v2 Section 4.3 newly specifies two generations per sample across 100 subsets for its diversity analysis, adding limited repeat-generation information. This is not repeated-training evidence. Neither version provides seeds, uncertainty intervals, error bars or a specified statistical test supporting its significance language.

E6.justification: v2 adds LIDC, SwinUNETR, NSD, histogram-control and latent-comparator results. The cardiac nnU-Net baseline changes from MI/PMO Dice 69.67/36.89 in v1 Table 1 to 68.61/36.32 in v2 Table 2, while shared augmented-training scores such as 70.34/43.54 remain unchanged. LV and myocardium scores disappear. The unexplained baseline revision should not be interpreted as a demonstrated performance change under verified identical conditions.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix C adds a mathematical account combining original and control histograms through a scaled log-space relation and exponentiation (Equations 5–6). v1 has diffusion objectives but no corresponding histogram model. This is a limited mathematical addition, without a new theorem or rigorous proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden the contribution from cardiac multi-class lesion synthesis to controllable pathology synthesis across MRI and CT. v2 explicitly claims handling multi-peak textures, controlling mask size and location, and benefiting both nnU-Net and SwinUNETR. The central background-preserving, lesion-focused claim is retained.

C2.justification: v2 identifies and explains a limitation of unconditioned LeFusion: healthy lung backgrounds bias generated nodules toward subtle, background-like appearances. It interprets histogram conditioning as shifting texture distributions and preventing this failure, while explaining its limited additional benefit for cardiac lesions through their smaller contrast differences. These are substantive new applicability and mechanism discussions.

D1.justification: New Appendix F documents crop/padding dimensions, A100 hardware, software versions, MONAI implementations, 200-epoch segmentation training, and training/inference times. Section 4.1 also describes fine-tuning the latent comparator's pretrained implementation. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1; they do not establish that retained experiments changed settings. The code/model access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through dedicated related-work sections covering large-volume medical generation, Blended-Diffusion and concurrent lesion-synthesis approaches. It distinguishes Chen et al.'s latent implementation more explicitly and explains comparison limitations. Several earlier citations, including MedMNIST and airway-topology repair, are removed; Chen et al.'s publication update alone is not a new citation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around controllable pathology synthesis. Background and concurrent-work discussions become dedicated related-work sections, the method narrative is reorganized around background preservation and texture/mask control, and the formerly visualization-only appendix becomes Sections A–F. These exceed local wording or numbering edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds an overview diagram, histogram plots and lung examples, revises both method diagrams, and restructures segmentation tables around two downstream models. The quality table moves to Appendix D and expands. Earlier cardiac mask and appendix visualizations are retained as Figures A2 and A6–A8, rather than newly introduced. The document also adopts a different layout and table-highlighting scheme.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the earlier paper's narrow empirical support through lung CT validation, a second segmentation architecture, additional comparators and controlled investigations of a texture-generation failure. Appendix F materially improves reproducibility. These gains outweigh the unexplained cardiac baseline revision, lost normal-region scores and remaining uncertainty-reporting gaps, although those weaknesses limit confidence in some performance claims.
